title: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction reference family
reaction: CO2 + n H2O + hν -> products (CO, CH4, CH3OH, HCOOH, ...) + n O2 (overall photocatalytic CO2 reduction)
objective: Optional literature-backed family for solar-driven CO2 photo-reduction. Candidates compare a TiO2 photocatalyst anchor (the canonical UV reference), a g-C3N4 / SnS2 Z-scheme visible-light option, and an MOF / Cu2O ternary heterojunction emerging route. Note: photocatalytic CO2 reduction differs from the photocatalytic water splitting family by product target (CO2 -> hydrocarbons / CO instead of H2 / O2).

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance photocatalyst cost, evidence quality, route maturity, and reported solar-to-hydrocarbon performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward photocatalyst cost while preserving route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward stronger literature support and reproducible photocatalyst preparation routes.

route_templates.name: TiO2 photocatalyst CO2-reduction route
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Bulk TiO2 photocatalyst preparation for CO2 reduction
postprocess: Surface modification (Pt or Cu cocatalyst optional)
quality_gates: CO2 reduction yield hold under UV
route_templates.route_note: Most transferable photocatalyst basis for CO2 reduction; UV-only activity limits solar-to-hydrocarbon performance.

route_templates.name: g-C3N4 / SnS2 Z-scheme route
preprocess: Sn and S precursor balancing for SnS2
route_templates.route_note: Z-scheme g-C3N4 / SnS2 route, attractive when visible-light operation is required and tunable redox-band alignment is desired.

route_templates.name: Cu2O / MOF heterojunction route
preprocess: Cu precursor balancing for Cu2O growth
route_templates.route_note: MOF-derived Cu2O heterojunction route, an emerging high-surface-area option whose route maturity and MOF cost are the main risks.

candidates.title: TiO2 photocatalyst (UV anchor)
candidates.summary: Bulk TiO2 photocatalyst, the canonical UV anchor for CO2 photo-reduction; product slate biased toward CO and CH4.
decision_notes: Most transferable photocatalyst basis for CO2 reduction screening.
UV-only activity caps solar-to-product performance versus visible-light variants.

pricing.note: Anatase TiO2 cost held on engineering proxy comparable to commercial photocatalyst-grade titania (matches PWC family).

candidates.title: g-C3N4 / SnS2 Z-scheme
candidates.summary: g-C3N4 / SnS2 direct Z-scheme heterojunction for visible-light-driven CO2 reduction, biased toward CO and methanol products.
decision_notes: Best fit when visible-light operation is required and metal-free polymer + sulfide stack is acceptable.
Heterojunction reproducibility and SnS2 stability under irradiation are the main route-maturity concerns.

pricing.note: g-C3N4 cost held on derived screening proxy reflecting nitrogen-precursor and pyrolysis overhead.
Sn pricing via market feed with a precursor / conversion markup for SnS2 active phase.

candidates.title: Cu2O / MOF heterojunction
candidates.summary: Cu2O / MOF ternary heterojunction photocatalyst with high CO2 adsorption capacity, biased toward methanol and CH4 products.
decision_notes: Best fit when high CO2 adsorption capacity is the program target.
MOF cost and Cu2O surface stability under photocatalysis remain the main risks.

pricing.note: Live Cu feed with a precursor / conversion markup for Cu2O active phase.
MOF host cost held on a derived screening proxy reflecting linker / metal-cluster synthesis overhead.
